title: Tero's remark to Merlin Sheldrake on mushrooms at the start and end of forest life cycles

tellings.quote: Not just mushrooms, but other really sacred foods tend to live in these like the beginning of the forest lifecycle, or at the end of the forest lifecycle, where there's extremely nothing else growing almost, like pioneer, or at the end of it when there's massive biodiversity.

plain: Mushrooms and other sacred foods tend to grow either at the very start of a forest's life cycle, when almost nothing else is growing, or at its end, when there is huge biodiversity, according to a mushroom specialist named Tero Isokauppila. He says he made this remark himself to Merlin Sheldrake, a biologist who studies fungi, and offers it as a hint that these foods play a special role in nature.
